_comment_1_when_to_use_this: OPTIONAL and manual. Nothing in this marketplace writes this file for you — project-kickoff deliberately does not, because which plugins a developer has enabled is user-level configuration (~/.claude/settings.json), not something a scaffold should decide for whoever clones the repo next. Copy this into a PRODUCT repo's .claude/settings.json and commit it ONLY if you want teammates to get these plugins automatically on clone. If you just want them for yourself, enable them in ~/.claude/settings.json instead and ignore this file.
_comment_2_access: If the 'github' source below is a private repo, anyone who clones a repo carrying this file needs read access to it (and `gh auth login` or a git credential helper) or they get an unresolvable marketplace and none of the skills. Never commit a local {"source": "directory"} path to a shared repo — it resolves on exactly one machine.
_comment_3_trim_this: Trim enabledPlugins to what the repo actually is. Engineering repos: frontend-only repos don't need backend, backend-only repos don't need frontend or design-system; architecture-foundations, codebase-map and deployment are cheap to leave on for anything. Delivery (PDP) plugins belong in an engagement workspace rather than a product codebase, so they are off by default here.
_comment_4_permissions: The codebase-map cache lives at ~/.claude/kaizen/, outside the repo, so without these it prompts for approval every session. Paths use '~/' deliberately — it resolves per-user, so this works unchanged on every machine and OS. Never replace it with an absolute path like C:/Users/<name>/, which grants nothing on anyone else's machine.
